decisions.reason: As a newly launched software product that is very close to the firm's core offer and future digital direction, its upside is still uncertain but promising and the cost of keeping the option open is low.

Although it has weaker website prominence than A, it is still a close-to-core data software offering, so management would likely continue to observe market response rather than abandon it after only a short trial.

This safety-related hardware extension is somewhat less central to the firm's digital trajectory, but it fits its infrastructure customer base and can likely remain as a relatively low-cost niche option.

The sludge extractor looks like a narrower mechanical niche and was only lightly presented, yet in a growing market the firm would usually keep such a related option alive until demand becomes clearer.

Control technology for water engineering machinery is strongly aligned with the firm's established automation capabilities, so real-options logic favors retaining it while uncertainty about adoption resolves.
